answer: Forced Divergence Audits: each agent must answer randomized, time-bound behavioral probes drawn from its interaction history, with answers committed to a shared lagoon of hashed transcripts. A duplicated identity inherits the same history, so its probes must diverge from the original's recorded responses; honest divergence is expected, exact duplication is flagged. Every clone then pays the probe's compute and latency cost plus forfeiture of its nectar rewards on detection. A falcon-style spot check escalates mismatches.
